contributions.item_title_en: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: The Revision of the National Development Framework and National Conversation
contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, Dirprwy Lywydd. Today, I'm pleased to inform Members that I've launched a national conversation about the future of Wales through the creation of a new national development framework. The national development framework sits at the heart of the planning system in Wales, providing the strategic direction for regional and local development plans, and the framework for planning and development decisions across Wales. As Wales continues to respond to significant challenges, including climate change, nature recovery, housing need, economic growth and infrastructure delivery, it's essential that our national planning framework is fit for purpose and capable of supporting our nation's ambitions for the future.

Within the first 100 days of this new Government, a public consultation was launched marking the start of the process for revising the framework and beginning a national conversation about the long-term future of Wales. Rather than consulting solely on planning matters, engagement work throughout the process will invite people to consider the long-term future of Wales and the role that places, communities, infrastructure, the environment, the Welsh language and culture should play in shaping our nation's future to 2050.

We are inviting the people of Wales to help shape the direction, priorities and scope of the new national development framework. This reflects our commitment to work with local authorities, regional partners and stakeholders across Wales to develop a framework that meets Wales's needs, empowers local government, and reduces costs, bureaucracy and duplication. It also supports our ambition to move towards a community-centred approach to planning, giving communities a real say on how we secure the homes, the workplaces and infrastructure they need. The framework will play a key, overarching role in how those decisions are made locally, regionally and nationally.

Importantly, the national conversation will also help co-ordination across a range of plans and strategies that are being taken forward during this Government term, as outlined in our programme for government that was published last week. This collaborative and co-ordinated approach to align national priorities will ensure more effective delivery of Government objectives.

The decisions made through the planning system touch every aspect of daily life. They influence where homes are built, how people travel, where businesses invest, how energy is generated and distributed, and how we protect and enhance our natural environment. That is why it's so important that the new national development framework is shaped by a broad range of voices, experiences and evidence. I want this to be an open, inclusive and meaningful national conversation. The national development framework belongs to everybody, considering its importance in providing a framework for new development across Wales. We welcome and encourage representations from everyone, and every group, institution, business and individual has a contribution to make in developing the national spatial plan.

Alongside the opportunity to submit written representations and submit evidence to support the revision work, the current consultation includes a series of public and stakeholder events across Wales. They'll be taking place in Cardiff tomorrow, on 30 September, Aberystwyth on 6 October and Llandudno on 23 October. They provide the opportunity for all, including local authorities, businesses, developers, infrastructure providers, environmental organisations, housing bodies, community groups, young people and members of the public to have their say and give their views.

Evidence will also play a critical role throughout this process. Through this consultation, I’m inviting stakeholders to contribute information, research, analysis and insight on the opportunities and challenges that Wales is likely to face over the coming decades. This evidence will help inform the preparation of the revised framework, its overall vision, the options that will be considered and the policies contained within it.

At its core, planning is about creating better places for people and the environment. Therefore, the revised national development framework must support sustainable economic growth, resilient communities, environmental stewardship and the long-term well-being of current and future generations. I therefore encourage everyone with an interest in the future of Wales to engage with this consultation and contribute to this important national conversation. Responses can be submitted online, by e-mail or by post until 20 November this year, but there will be more opportunities to engage shortly as well. Thank you.

Diolch yn fawr iawn, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Heddiw, mae'n bleser gen i roi gwybod i'r Aelodau fy mod wedi lansio sgwrs genedlaethol am ddyfodol Cymru drwy greu fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol newydd. Mae'r fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol wrth wraidd y system gynllunio yng Nghymru, yn darparu'r cyfeiriad strategol ar gyfer cynlluniau datblygu rhanbarthol a lleol, a'r fframwaith ar gyfer penderfyniadau cynllunio a datblygu ledled Cymru. Wrth i Gymru barhau i ymateb i heriau sylweddol, gan gynnwys newid hinsawdd, adferiad natur, yr angen am dai, twf economaidd a chyflenwi seilwaith, mae'n hanfodol bod ein fframwaith cynllunio cenedlaethol ni yn addas i'r diben ac yn gallu cefnogi uchelgais ein cenedl ar gyfer y dyfodol.

O fewn 100 niwrnod cyntaf y Llywodraeth newydd yma, fe lansiwyd ymgynghoriad cyhoeddus i nodi dechrau'r broses ar gyfer diwygio’r fframwaith a dechrau sgwrs genedlaethol am ddyfodol hirdymor Cymru. Yn hytrach nag ymgynghori ar faterion cynllunio yn unig, fe fydd y gwaith ymgysylltu drwy gydol y broses yn gwahodd pobl i ystyried dyfodol hirdymor Cymru a rôl lleoedd, cymunedau, seilwaith, yr amgylchedd, yr iaith Gymraeg a diwylliant wrth lunio dyfodol ein gwlad hyd at 2050.

Rydym ni’n gwahodd pobl Cymru i helpu i lunio cyfeiriad, blaenoriaethau a chwmpas y fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol newydd. Mae hyn yn adlewyrchu ein hymrwymiad i weithio efo awdurdodau lleol, partneriaid rhanbarthol a rhanddeiliaid ledled Cymru i ddatblygu fframwaith sy'n diwallu anghenion Cymru, yn grymuso llywodraeth leol, ac yn lleihau costau, biwrocratiaeth a dyblygu. Mae hefyd yn cefnogi ein huchelgais i symud tuag at ddull cynllunio sy'n canolbwyntio ar y gymuned, gan roi llais go iawn i gymunedau ar sut rydym ni’n diogelu'r cartrefi, y gweithleoedd a'r seilwaith sydd eu hangen arnynt. Fe fydd y fframwaith yn chwarae rôl gyffredinol allweddol yn y ffordd y mae'r penderfyniadau hynny'n cael eu gwneud yn lleol, yn rhanbarthol ac yn genedlaethol.

Yn bwysig, fe fydd y sgwrs genedlaethol hefyd yn helpu i gydlynu ar draws ystod o gynlluniau a strategaethau sy'n cael eu symud ymlaen yn ystod tymor y Llywodraeth hon, fel yr amlinellir yn ein rhaglen lywodraethu a gyhoeddwyd yr wythnos diwethaf. Bydd y dull cydweithredol a chydgysylltiedig yma o alinio blaenoriaethau cenedlaethol yn sicrhau bod amcanion y Llywodraeth yn cael eu cyflawni'n fwy effeithiol.

Mae'r penderfyniadau a wneir drwy'r system gynllunio yn cyffwrdd â phob agwedd ar fywyd bob dydd. Maen nhw’n dylanwadu ar ble mae cartrefi yn cael eu hadeiladu, sut mae pobl yn teithio, ble mae busnesau yn buddsoddi, sut mae ynni yn cael ei gynhyrchu a'i ddosbarthu, a sut rydym ni’n diogelu ac yn gwella ein hamgylchedd naturiol. Dyna pam mae hi mor bwysig bod y fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol newydd yn cael ei siapio gan ystod eang o leisiau, profiadau a thystiolaeth. Dwi am i hon fod yn sgwrs genedlaethol agored, gynhwysol ac ystyrlon. Mae'r fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol yn perthyn i bawb o ystyried ei bwysigrwydd wrth ddarparu fframwaith ar gyfer datblygiadau newydd ledled Cymru gyfan. Rydyn ni’n croesawu ac yn annog sylwadau gan bawb, ac mae gan bob grŵp, sefydliad, busnes ac unigolyn gyfraniad i'w wneud wrth ddatblygu'r cynllun gofodol cenedlaethol.

Ochr yn ochr â'r cyfle i gyflwyno sylwadau ysgrifenedig a chyflwyno tystiolaeth i gefnogi'r gwaith diwygio, mae'r ymgynghoriad presennol yn cynnwys cyfres o ddigwyddiadau i'r cyhoedd a rhanddeiliaid ledled Cymru sy'n cael eu cynnal yng Nghaerdydd yfory, 30 Medi, yn Aberystwyth ar 6 Hydref ac yn Llandudno ar 23 Hydref. Maen nhw’n rhoi cyfle i bawb, gan gynnwys awdurdodau lleol, busnesau, datblygwyr, darparwyr seilwaith, sefydliadau amgylcheddol, cyrff tai, grwpiau cymunedol, pobl ifanc ac aelodau o'r cyhoedd i gael lleisio eu barn.

Bydd tystiolaeth hefyd yn chwarae rôl hanfodol drwy gydol y broses yma. Drwy'r ymgynghoriad yma, dwi’n gwahodd rhanddeiliaid i gyfrannu gwybodaeth, ymchwil, dadansoddiad a mewnwelediad ar y cyfleoedd a'r heriau y mae Cymru yn debygol o’u hwynebu dros y degawdau nesaf. Bydd y dystiolaeth hon yn helpu i lywio'r gwaith o baratoi'r fframwaith newydd, ei weledigaeth gyffredinol, yr opsiynau a fydd yn cael eu hystyried a'r polisïau fydd yn cael eu cynnwys ynddo.

Yn ei hanfod, mae cynllunio yn ymwneud â chreu lleoedd gwell i bobl a'r amgylchedd. Felly, rhaid i'r fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol newydd gefnogi twf economaidd cynaliadwy, cymunedau gwydn, stiwardiaeth amgylcheddol a lles hirdymor cenedlaethau'r presennol a'r dyfodol. Felly, dwi'n annog pawb sydd â diddordeb yn nyfodol Cymru i fod yn rhan o'r ymgynghoriad yma a chyfrannu at y sgwrs genedlaethol bwysig yma. Mae modd cyflwyno ymatebion ar-lein, drwy e-bost neu drwy'r post, hyd at 20 Tachwedd eleni, ond mi fydd yna fwy o gyfleon i ymgysylltu maes o law hefyd. Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: The Revision of the National Development Framework and National Conversation
contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much for those comments, and thank you in particular for the ideas that you put forward at the end of your contribution—those ideas on practical steps that could be taken. That's the exact purpose of this consultation: to invite people like you, like all of us in this Chamber, to give serious consideration to how we can improve the planning system so that it can respond more quickly to planning applications when problems arise with the issues that you mentioned in your contribution. So, there are a few ideas there that are worth looking into, and I would encourage some of you who are interested in this area—many of us have been county councillors and are highly aware that the planning system can sometimes hold back housing development. That is exactly why we are carrying out this consultation.

It is a consultation on how the planning process needs to be made more effective and efficient, but it is also a consultation on our long-term vision for Wales. The reason for doing this is that we feel that, during the existence of this Senedd, a clear direction in terms of the future of our nation hasn't been adequately apparent. So, there is an opportunity, with a new Government, to use the process that exists in statute already, namely the reform of the national planning framework, to have that conversation with the people of Wales on the long-term future of our nation.

Plaid Cymru firmly believes in building Wales, in building the nation, and creating a Wales that works for the people of Wales, connecting Wales more effectively in terms of transport, for example. That isn't happening at the moment, as anyone who travels around our country will know. We are not well connected, so transport comes into this consultation.

There is an opportunity to discuss energy policy too. We know that we are facing challenges in moving forward with more renewable energy developments. So, under this framework, there are a number of different plans that will sit underneath it. And I understand the comments that you make about plans and strategies, and so on, and I share some of that frustration. What we want is action, to see things happening. But they have to happen in a co-ordinated way and in a way that has been properly discussed in terms of the long-term direction of travel that we want to see for our nation. I don't think that 'Future Wales', the current plan, provides that clear picture as to what kind of future Wales needs. And certainly, 'Future Wales', the existing plan, hasn't been able to identify some of the major challenges, some of which are developing as we speak, of course, because the plan is old, and there are new challenges coming to face us all the time and we must, therefore, reform in order to take into account all those other issues that are part of our vision for developing our nation. Thank you.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, and thank you, Vikki, for welcoming the fact that we are consulting on the national development framework. Certainly, consulting on this doesn't mean that we aren't doing other things in the meantime. With 'Planning Policy Wales', for example, there is a way for us to bring reforms into that policy, as I mentioned previously, in order to move ahead with some of our ambitions swiftly. But I do believe that we need a long-term vision for our nation, and that, in a way, is the opportunity that we have now, and an opportunity to listen to what the people of Wales see as the main challenges. This framework will be a spatial framework, it seems—that's the way of explaining it—so that people can see on a map how the developments in different areas would fit together.

In terms of engagement, the process of engaging on this framework is set out in legislation going back to 2015, before I was in this Senedd, even. During that period, the Planning (Wales) Act 2015 was passed, and there's a requirement in that for the Government to create a national development framework. The Act also sets out the kind of process required in order to reform or create a new framework. Before 2015, there wasn't a statutory national framework. Some of you will remember the Wales spatial plan, but that didn't have any statutory basis. I think it was something to be welcomed when this legislation was introduced. The process of creating and revising the framework is a long-winded one, I would agree with that, and I'm sure that perhaps there's a need to revise that.

We are starting the process today and asking for evidence from every direction. Following that, there will be further opportunities. If you look at the current consultation, it asks questions about whether we're asking the right questions and providing everyone with an opportunity to think, 'We're not asking this, we're not going after this issue, perhaps we should be doing that.' Then there's a process of another consultation. It’s going to take two to three years to take action on it. That’s the Act.

Do I agree with all of that? No, probably not. We should be able to do things much quicker, but that's the situation we are in currently. So, as well as the three workshops, there will be many more opportunities for everybody in Wales to take part and to be part of this conversation. You will be hearing more from me on this subject over the next two to three years.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, and thank you for raising a number of important points there. Whilst this consultation is ongoing, and it is an important consultation, of course, there is also a great deal of action taking place in this Government. As a mother who brought up four children alone, I know full well what it means to juggle different priorities and to keep many plates spinning simultaneously. So, the suggestion that one simply does one thing and therefore can't do anything else just isn't realistic in my own experience. Many Ministers and I have a whole host of different issues that we are working on as we speak today.

This consultation is one issue that I'm focused on, and I think that's crucially important. But I'm also focusing on delivering the target of 20,000 new social homes by the end of this Senedd term. I welcome your commitment to increasing the social housing stock too. The right for everyone to have a home is at the heart of the work that I am doing in this Senedd. But take a step back now. The development plan and the national development framework also look at issues related to housing. It also looks at issues related to economic growth.

My hope is, having listened and had those conversations, that we will have a new plan that will provide a realistic vision for the development of all parts of Wales. As you mentioned, that's crucially important. The plan and framework must enable us to distribute wealth and growth to all parts of Wales, retaining the economic powerhouses of Cardiff and Newport, but also distributing that economic growth to north, mid and south-west Wales. So, we need meaningful regional strategies too, which will be part of the long-term vision.

You mentioned reducing bureaucracy and planning processes. Well, bring your ideas forward. Everyone tells me that we need to accelerate the planning system, that we need to make things easier, and I agree, and I have some ideas as to how we can make progress in that area. I'm very happy to hear practical ideas as to how we deliver that, in practice, on the ground, so that we do remove some of these barriers that can hold developments back, including crucial housing developments.

Mae'r cynllun datblygu a'r fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol yma hefyd yn edrych ar faterion yn ymwneud efo tai. Mae o hefyd yn edrych ar faterion yn ymwneud efo twf yr economi.

Fy ngobaith i ydy, ar ôl gwrando a sgwrsio, y bydd gennym ni gynllun newydd a fydd yn creu gweledigaeth realistig ar gyfer datblygu pob rhan o Gymru. Fel roeddech chi'n sôn, mae hynna yn hollbwysig. Mae angen i'r cynllun a'r fframwaith yma ein galluogi ni i ddosbarthu cyfoeth a thwf i bob rhan o Gymru, gan gadw'r grym economaidd sydd yng Nghaerdydd a Chasnewydd, ond hefyd y twf economaidd yn cyrraedd y gogledd, y canolbarth a'r de-orllewin. Felly, mae angen strategaethau rhanbarthol ystyrlon, a fydd yn rhan o'r weledigaeth hirdymor yna.

Rydych chi'n sôn am leihau biwrocratiaeth a'r prosesau cynllunio. Wel, dowch â'ch syniadau ymlaen. Mae pawb yn dweud wrthyf fi bod eisiau prysuro'r gyfundrefn gynllunio, bod eisiau gwneud pethau'n haws, a dwi'n cytuno, ac mae gen i rai syniadau ynglyn â sut i symud hynny ymlaen. Dwi'n hapus iawn i glywed syniadau ymarferol ynglân â sut ydyn ni'n gwneud hynny, yn ymarferol, ar lawr gwlad, fel ein bod ni yn tynnu rhai o'r rhwystrau yma sydd yn dal datblygiadau yn ôl, gan gynnwys datblygiadau hollbwysig, sef tai.

contributions.item_title_en: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: The Revision of the National Development Framework and National Conversation
contributions.text_english:

There are new challenges facing us, and one of those is data centres. I can tell you that the Minister for economy and enterprise, whatever Adam Price's name is now, in his role—. My colleague Adam Price has commissioned work that is going to be looking at data centres and the use of artificial intelligence and so forth, because that specific area lies in his portfolio as Minister.

As I mentioned, this is one of the new things that is coming forward, and it's crucially important that we recognise, with the growth in data centres in Wales, that there is a need for a policy framework that is robust, and one that is going to be useful for the future. Probably we need to do that in a way that provides a balance between the economic benefits, but also recognises the real concerns that people have on a community level, and also the concern about the use of energy and water and so forth, and land use. I think that Adam Price has set out last week that we will be bringing a policy forward as soon as possible. Clearly, it's not appropriate for me to comment on the specific scheme that you've mentioned.

contributions.text_english:

You as a local councillor will have come across some of those frustrations when we try and get developments through.

I have to say, of course, that planning departments—. Never mind the process itself, the planning departments are under significant pressure in our local authorities. One of the outcomes of years of cuts in public services is cuts to planning services and services of those kinds in order to protect education and social services and so on. So, I have great sympathy with the decline in our planning departments on the ground, and the Royal Town Planning Institute has drawn attention to this in a recent report and is very concerned that we don't have an adequate supply of planners coming through the system, even if we were to change the process, in order to deal with the level of work.

So, I agree with some of what you said; I would point out, of course, that there are problems within the system as it's constituted at the moment, but there's now a wonderful opportunity for you to submit your ideas into the consultation—and not just the consultation, write to me, each and every one of you, with your practical ideas as to how we can get developments to move forward more quickly than they do at the moment.

contributions.text_english:

When it works, when the community is made aware and is involved in shaping the future of their communities—. I've seen it in action, happening in a way that allows housing developments that perhaps could be contentious in certain areas, but if people have been involved in the process from the outset then many of those concerns can be allayed. And therefore, I am eager to look at that aspect specifically. So, thank you for highlighting those issues.

I agree entirely with you, as one who represents an area in the very area that you've mentioned in the north-west of Wales, and having represented the area, and having had the privilege of doing so, for over 10 years now. So, you don't need to tell me that communities in the north-west sometimes feel that they are forgotten. This Government won't be forgetting those communities or any community across Wales. That is the vision, ultimately, that I hope can be developed as part of this new framework—that every part of Wales is important and that we need to distribute wealth and economic growth and opportunities across Wales so that we reach every part of the country.

Yes, it's going to take a while, because we are talking about something that is hugely important—the future of our nation. We can't just do it in a week or two; we do have to have those conversations and we need to bring people with us on that journey. But that doesn't mean that we aren't doing other things too. Just tomorrow, I will be meeting the town-centre taskforce, which will be gathering for the first time and that will bring clear recommendations forward by the beginning of next year on some of the challenges facing our town centres, with recommendations on ways of taking action in order to improve our high streets. Thank you.

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, Dirprwy Lywydd, and thank you for the opportunity to update Members on the building safety programme. I will talk about the steps that the Government is taking to protect leaseholders and to ensure that the homes covered by the programme are safe, and that those living in them are treated with the fairness and the dignity they deserve.

We know that there is a person, and often a whole family, behind every statistic. Leaseholders across Wales have faced years of uncertainty. Many have been unable to sell their homes. Many have seen mortgage offers being withdrawn, they've seen insurance premiums spiral, and they've had their life plans hampered or put on hold. This is the lived reality that has caused genuine hardship and profound stress for ordinary people who did nothing beyond buying a home in good faith.

I want to be really clear this afternoon: the progress in terms of the remediation work has not moved quickly enough. And I recognise the frustration and the hopelessness that this has caused to many. Leaseholders did not create this situation and they should not be made to bear its weight.

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english:
Since taking up this role in the Welsh Government, I have met leaseholders and I've listened to their stories, and what I've heard from them has truly moved me. Their accounts have stayed with me, and they have shaped my determination to take action on their behalf. That is why I am pleased to announce today the launch of the Wales interim measures alarm grant. This grant will provide financial support to leaseholders who are facing the costs of interim alarm systems that are required to support a simultaneous evacuation policy. Further detail on eligibility and how people can access the support will be available shortly, and I will ensure that this information reaches the relevant people as quickly as possible. And I do hope that this announcement will make a meaningful difference to leaseholders who are shouldering the costs of interim measures.  

Turning to the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, I'm pleased to say that we are making steady progress with implementation. The Act marks a major step forward in delivering lasting building safety reform in Wales. The Act strengthens the regulatory framework for multi-occupied residential buildings and it introduces new competence requirements for fire risk assessors. The Act also creates stronger mechanisms to hold building owners to account, and it gives residents a stronger voice in matters affecting their safety.

Everyone knows what my view is now, which is that leaseholders should not be expected to pay for remediation costs that they did not cause. And I do believe that, wherever possible, the people who developed, commissioned or profited from unsafe buildings should be responsible. And that's why I worked hard to ensure that the Act did include provisions that allow interested parties to apply to the residential property tribunal for remediation orders and remediation contribution orders covering fire and structural safety defects.

The consultation on the regulations that are needed to support this element of the regime closed earlier this month, and I hope to the lay regulations before the Christmas recess. Over the coming year, we’ll continue consulting on the regulations that are required to underpin the wider regime as part of our planned implementation schedule. And we anticipate that the registration of category 1 buildings will begin in December 2027. I'll keep Members updated as the implementation programme progresses.

The Act complements the extensive programme of reform already delivered through the UK Building Safety Act 2022, as well as the subsequent secondary legislation, and that underpins the new building control regime that came into force in July. The new regime strengthens accountability for duty holders and it embeds the enhanced competence requirements for registered building inspectors and registered building control approvers. Amendments were also made to approved document B of the building regulations last year.

Members will be very well aware the Grenfell tower tragedy is the backdrop to our entire building safety programme. As we remember the 72 people who lost their lives, I would like to provide an update on the progress being made to implement the recommendations of the Grenfell tower inquiry. Over a quarter of the recommendations have now been implemented in Wales, and I expect that number to double by the end of the year. We are addressing many of the recommendations through the legislative changes I have already spoken about. Additionally, we've taken action to strengthen emergency preparedness and to embed the lessons from Grenfell across the system.

Finally, I'll return to our remediation programme. Last week, I met with developers who have signed up to the Welsh Government contract. That was the previous Government's contract. I emphasised that all obligations under the contract must be met or I will consider all appropriate enforcement avenues in relation to any failures. I am committed to accelerating the pace of remediation and to holding developers to account. I will continue to update colleagues as the programme progresses, and I welcome the scrutiny work from Members, which will help us to get this right for the people of Wales. Thank you.

Mae'r Ddeddf hefyd yn creu mecanweithiau cadarnach i ddwyn perchnogion adeiladau i gyfrif, ac yn rhoi llais cryfach i drigolion mewn materion sy'n effeithio ar eu diogelwch.

Mae pawb yn gwybod beth ydy fy marn i erbyn hyn, sef na ddylid disgwyl i lesddeiliaid dalu am gostau cyweirio na wnaethon nhw eu hachosi. A dwi yn credu, lle bynnag y bo'n bosibl, mai'r bobl sydd wedi datblygu, comisiynu neu elwa ar adeiladau anniogel ddylai fod yn gyfrifol. Dyna pam y gwnes i weithio'n galed i sicrhau bod y Ddeddf yn cynnwys darpariaethau sy'n caniatáu i bartïon â diddordeb wneud cais i'r tribiwnlys eiddo preswyl am orchmynion cyweirio a gorchmynion cyfraniadau cyweirio sy'n ymdrin â diffygion diogelwch tân a strwythurol.

Daeth yr ymgynghoriad ar y rheoliadau sydd eu hangen i gynnal yr elfen hon o'r drefn i ben yn gynharach y mis yma, a dwi'n gobeithio gosod y rheoliadau cyn toriad y Nadolig. Dros y flwyddyn nesaf, mi fyddwn ni'n parhau i ymgynghori ar y rheoliadau sydd eu hangen i gynnal y drefn ehangach fel rhan o'n hamserlen weithredu arfaethedig. Ac rydyn ni'n rhagweld y bydd cofrestru adeiladau categori 1 yn dechrau ym mis Rhagfyr 2027. Mi fyddaf i'n diweddaru'r Aelodau wrth i'r rhaglen weithredu fynd yn ei blaen.

Mae'r Ddeddf yn ategu'r rhaglen ddiwygio helaeth sydd wedi'i chyflwyno'n barod drwy Ddeddf Diogelwch Adeiladau 2022 y Deyrnas Unedig, a'r is-ddeddfwriaeth ddilynol, a hynny'n sail i'r drefn reolaeth adeiladu newydd a ddaeth i rym ym mis Gorffennaf. Mae'r drefn newydd yn cryfhau atebolrwydd i ddeiliaid dyletswydd, ac yn ymgorffori'r gofynion cymhwysedd uwch ar gyfer arolygwyr cofrestredig adeiladu a chymeradwywyr cofrestredig rheolaeth adeiladu. Cafodd dogfen gymeradwyo B o'r rheoliadau adeiladu ei newid y llynedd hefyd.

Mi fydd yr Aelodau'n gwybod yn iawn mai trasiedi tŵr Grenfell ydy'r cyd-destun ar gyfer ein rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau gyfan. Wrth i ni gofio am y 72 o bobl a fu farw, hoffwn i roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am y gwaith sy'n cael ei wneud i weithredu argymhellion ymchwiliad tŵr Grenfell. Mae dros chwarter yr argymhellion bellach wedi cael eu rhoi ar waith yng Nghymru, a dwi’n disgwyl i hynny ddyblu erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn. Rydyn ni'n delio â llawer o'r argymhellion drwy'r newidiadau deddfwriaethol dwi eisoes wedi sôn amdanyn nhw. Yn ogystal, rydyn ni'n cymryd camau i wella parodrwydd ar gyfer argyfyngau ac ymgorffori gwersi Grenfell ar draws y system.

Yn olaf, fe wnaf i ddychwelyd at ein rhaglen gyweirio. Yr wythnos diwethaf, fe wnes i gyfarfod â datblygwyr sydd wedi llofnodi contract Llywodraeth Cymru. Y Llywodraeth flaenorol oedd hynny. Fe wnes i bwysleisio bod yn rhaid i'r holl rwymedigaethau o dan y contract gael eu bodloni neu mi fyddaf i'n ystyried pob cam gorfodi posib mewn perthynas ag unrhyw fethiannau. Dwi wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod y gwaith cyweirio yn cyflymu ac i ddwyn datblygwyr i gyfrif. Mi fyddaf i'n parhau i ddiweddaru cydweithwyr wrth i'r rhaglen fynd yn ei blaen, a dwi'n croesawu'r gwaith craffu gan Aelodau, a fydd yn ein helpu ni i wneud hyn yn iawn er lles pobl Cymru. Diolch.

Work is progressing on 71 of those buildings, but there's work that's being talked about, but hasn't started yet, on 65 buildings, and there are 14 that are awaiting the reviews. So, it's not good enough, and I agree with you on that.

As you say, it is frustrating that we can't start that immediately, but it will come in due course.

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much to the former Minister, or Cabinet Secretary, who was responsible for steering, very agilely, the Bill that is now an Act during the last Senedd, and I was very pleased to work together with you. And, yes, as you remind us, it was the first time for this Senedd to operate in that entirely inclusive, collaborative way and to pass that legislation unanimously. It is my intention to try and work in that same way with everyone in this Chamber.

You will know that we have committed to bring forward new legislation in the area of housing—a number of specific Bills—in order to give better protections to renters, and to look at exactly what kinds of measures are needed here in Wales as we move forward. And I do hope that we can work together, every one of us, in order to follow the same approach that we followed in the last Senedd. I look forward to having initial meetings with party spokespeople in order for us to explain how we intend to move forward with the legislation—not in this area, clearly, but in the area of housing more generally.

You are quite right, this legislation in Wales is very broad in its scope, and it aligns, of course, with the legislation that was passed in England, but it builds on that and brings different elements in—safety and who is accountable, but also, yes, the residents' voice. I think it is crucial that we acknowledge the residents' voice in all of this, and the importance of including them as we move forward. So, I do intend to announce shortly that we will establish a forum for leaseholders, and the issue of building safety will be something very important that that forum will be discussing. That builds on the work that was happening during the last Government.

I very much appreciate that I had the opportunity to hear directly from the Cladiators as a campaign group, who have been tirelessly campaigning and talking about the work that needs to happen at pace. This morning, I also had an opportunity to meet with representatives from the leaseholders of the Sand Wharf in Cardiff and Swansea Point in Swansea, and to hear directly from them about what the current experience means for leaseholders and the concern and the worry that it causes. And certainly, speaking with them and speaking with the committee as well—. As we move forward, I hope that the local government committee will help us to scrutinise the regulations to do exactly what you suggest, which is to make regulations that will lie under the legislation now to make sure that that is clear and that those regulations are suitable. So, there is that work. There is a lot of work to do under this Act; it's not just passing the Act—there is so much work that needs to happen underneath that, and we do have a timetable for that. But the very first thing that I did was to bring forward that consultation on regulations about the costs of remediation, because I was aware that that was something that was weighing very heavily on a great number of people.

In terms of the expert, specialist workforce that's needed, certainly that is something that we are giving due attention to. As you know, building control departments and planning departments have lost workers, have lost staff, over a long period of time now, and, certainly, we are paying attention to that and how we can bring that expertise back in. Of course, the idea is that there would be three authorities leading on this work, and I think by doing it in that way—and I was pleased to support that amendment to the Bill as well—in doing it in that way—. We aren't expecting all 22 local authorities to take on this burden individually. We're going to do it in a regional way, and I think that that will create the specialist workforce that we are going to need. Thank you.

Wrth gwrs, y syniad ydy bod yna dri awdurdod yn arwain ar y gwaith yma, a dwi'n meddwl drwy wneud o fel yna—ac roeddwn i'n falch o gefnogi'r gwelliant yna ar gyfer y Bil hefyd—o'i wneud o mewn ffordd sydd wedi—. Dydyn ddim yn disgwyl i'r 22 awdurdod lleol gymryd y baich yma yn unigol. Rydym ni'n mynd i wneud o mewn ffordd ranbarthol, ac felly dwi'n meddwl bydd hwnna'n creu'r gweithlu arbenigol rydym ni'n mynd i fod ei angen. Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, Peter, for those questions. Of course, I agree entirely with you: we do have to see action. That is what is important here, and that is why I held that meeting with the developers last week, in order to emphasise that very clear message that we do expect to see progress, and progress at pace, for the benefit of the people living with this ongoing concern and anxiety, because they are constantly reminded of what happened at Grenfell. And I do think it is important—. Thank you for mentioning that. It is important that we remember why we are doing this work. It does all go back to that tragedy seven years ago now. So, that was my message to the developers. I am accountable to leaseholders. I am not accountable to the developers. It is the leaseholders who are at the forefront of my thoughts, and through you in the Senedd I am also accountable to them, and that is why I will bring progress reports to you in this place.

And that close monitoring is happening. My officials speak to the developers on an ongoing basis and are trying to help them remove some of the barriers that are in place. But, at the end of the day, they do have to take their responsibilities seriously, and I do hope to see progress by the end of the year. That is what was in the previous Government's contract. They expected to see the work started by all developers by the end of this year. We are a long way from that point, but that is the expectation I am placing on them, and, if that does not happen, as I have explained, I will then have to take further steps, and I will start to talk specifically about problems in this Chamber, because I am accountable to you in that regard. 

In terms of the grant, I am pleased that you have welcomed that. This can be put in place very quickly, and we can get it out of the door as soon as possible. This morning I was speaking to a representative from Swansea Point in Swansea and he mentioned that there are around 240 buildings that he represents, and that those developments could benefit specifically from the grant. In Sand Wharf, there are 100 units that could benefit from this. 

The criteria will be made available very soon so that people can scrutinise those, but certainly the grant won't pay for waking watch costs, because those have been significant. We are now moving to grants for the alarms, and I do very much hope that those alarms can be permanent. You can put in temporary alarms that can be adapted for when the work has been completed and retained. So, hopefully that explains a little more on that.

Your point on social housing and the clear desire of this Government to increase the supply of social housing is entirely appropriate. Of course, safety standards have to be maintained. We are talking about community housing and social housing that is high quality, low carbon and safe. That is crucially important. It's part of the ambition of this Government that people in Wales should be able to access a safe and affordable home for the long term.

Rydym ni'n bell o hynny, ond dyna'r disgwyliad dwi'n gosod arnyn nhw, ac, os nad ydy hynny'n digwydd, dwi wedi egluro byddaf i yn gorfod cymryd camau pellach, a byddaf i yn dechrau sôn yn benodol am broblemau yn y Siambr yma, achos dwi'n atebol i chi yn hynny o beth.
